Q: Using ffmpeg to display a static image if an RTMP input source is missing A:

I was having the same failure to resume my RTMP stream after I stopped it.

  1. Instead of creating an input RTMP stream I created an input HLS stream using the following muxer syntax:

    -f hls -hls_list_size 30 -hls_time 10 -hls_flags delete_segments R:\temp.m3u8

  2. I hosted my m3u8 file on a web server with the domain hlsserver.com.

  3. I fed this to another FFmpeg command and simply remuxed the HLS stream to RTMP:

    ffmpeg -i https://www.hlsserver.com/temp.m3u8 -c copy -f flv rtmp://@127.0.0.1:5130/live/test/liveStream`

It was now possible to resume playback after stopping the initial stream. This method was also easier on system resources than the OP's command.

Q: SQL procedure that won't work for some reason A:

Since you are using JSON (json_array_append, json_table), you can use these tools and not implement string_split at all.

CREATE PROCEDURE `new_procedure6`(
    IN variants VARCHAR(50)
)
BEGIN
    with src as(
    SELECT variant_number,
      count(variant_number)over() validated,
      count(*)over()-count(variant_number)over()  not_validated
    FROM JSON_TABLE(concat('["',replace(concat('3,1,',variants),',','","'),'"]')
       , '$[*]' 
        COLUMNS (variant_number INT PATH '$')) AS variant_number
    )
    select * from src
    where variant_number is not null
    ;
END ;

call new_procedure6('1,v7,vb,9');

Output:

+----------------+-----------+---------------+
| variant_number | validated | not_validated |
+----------------+-----------+---------------+
|              3 |         4 |             2 |
|              1 |         4 |             2 |
|              1 |         4 |             2 |
|              9 |         4 |             2 |
+----------------+-----------+---------------+

Delimiter in example is ,.
Fiddle

Upd1 This method can be used when the question is "how to turn string - list of values separated by a delimiter, into a table of values"

set @variants="2,v7,vb,9";

SELECT rn,variant_number
FROM JSON_TABLE( concat('["',replace(@variants,',','","'),'"]')
       , '$[*]' 
        COLUMNS (
              rn FOR ORDINALITY,
              variant_number varchar(10) PATH '$'
            )
     ) AS variant_number

Output is

rn variant_number
1 2
2 v7
3 vb
4 9

FROM myTable t
WHERE t.id IN(

Q: Remove video from Plex's "Recently Added" section A:

I updated the script above to work for TV shows (core show and episodes) and movies. It also asks what you want to do, and checks it selected the thing you want.

from plexapi.server import PlexServer
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

# Prompt for media type
print("What type of media?")
print("  1. TV Show")
print("  2. Movie")
media_choice = input("\nEnter number: ").strip()

if media_choice == '1':
    media_type = 'tv'
    library = 'TV Shows'
elif media_choice == '2':
    media_type = 'movie'
    library = 'Movies'
else:
    print("Invalid selection.")
    exit(1)

# Prompt for title
title = input("Enter title: ")

# Connect to your Plex server
baseurl = "http://localhost:32400"
x-plex-token = "nnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnn" #Get this from cookies / site inspection
plex = PlexServer(baseurl, x-plex-token)

# Search for matching titles
results = plex.library.section(library).search(title)

if not results:
    print(f"No titles found matching '{title}'.")
    exit(1)

# Try exact match first (case-insensitive)
exact = [r for r in results if r.title.lower() == title.lower()]

if len(exact) == 1:
    media = exact[0]
elif len(exact) > 1:
    print(f"\nMultiple exact matches found:")
    for i, result in enumerate(exact, start=1):
        print(f"  {i}. {result.title} ({result.year})")
    choice = int(input("\nEnter number to select: "))
    if choice < 1 or choice > len(exact):
        print("Invalid selection.")
        exit(1)
    media = exact[choice - 1]
else:
    print(f"\nNo exact match found. Partial matches:")
    for i, result in enumerate(results, start=1):
        print(f"  {i}. {result.title} ({result.year})")
    choice = int(input("\nEnter number to select, or 0 to exit: "))
    if choice < 1 or choice > len(results):
        print("Exiting.")
        exit(1)
    media = results[choice - 1]

# Show confirmation and prompt for days
print(f"\nFound: '{media.title}' ({media.year})")
days = int(input("Enter number of days in the past: "))

if media_type == 'tv':
    print(f"This will update the show and all episodes to {days} days ago.")
else:
    print(f"This will update the movie to {days} days ago.")
confirm = input("\nProceed? (y/n): ").strip().lower()

if confirm != 'y':
    print("Cancelled.")
    exit(0)

print(f"\nUpdating '{media.title}'...")

# Define a date in the past
old_date = datetime.now() - timedelta(days=days)
old_date_str = old_date.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')

# Update addedAt on the main title
media.edit(**{'addedAt.value': old_date_str})

# If TV show, also update all episodes
if media_type == 'tv':
    for episode in media.episodes():
        episode.edit(**{'addedAt.value': old_date_str})
    print(f"TV Show '{media.title}' updated added date for all episodes to hide from recent.")
else:
    print(f"Movie '{media.title}' updated added date to hide from recent.")
